title: Ada and the Orchard
premise: In 1913 Kent, Ivo Underhill drives for suffragist Edith Marlowe and secretly reads the letters he delivers, convinced history belongs to other people. When a stranger named Ada arrives bearing a letter in the handwriting of Edith's brother Julian — officially dead at Loos two years earlier — Ivo and Ada uncover that Julian faked his death to escape court-martial and has been living under a false name in enemy territory, sending coded appeals through Ada. As war bureaucracy closes in and Edith's movement makes her a target, the three must honor a peacetime promise Julian made to protect a German friend's family, forcing Ivo to choose between loyalty, law, and the found family he never expected. The novel ends at the century's turn of 1917 into 1918: Julian surrenders himself to save Ada from prosecution, Edith wins her promise's fulfillment through political leverage, and Ivo finally accepts that history happened to him all along.
about_author: C. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in county record offices. Their fiction is known for finding the extraordinary in the hands of ordinary letter-carriers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Words
chapters.summary: Ivo Underhill, driver and reluctant reader of sealed letters, introduces his philosophy: history happens elsewhere. He delivers Edith Marlowe's suffrage correspondence through Kent villages. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: comfortable detachment about to crack.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: A rain-soaked young woman, Ada, arrives at Marlowe House asking for Edith by a childhood nickname no stranger should know. She carries a worn letter she refuses to surrender. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: Edith recognizes the letter's script as her brother Julian's — killed at Loos in 1915. Ada claims he wrote it six weeks ago. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: grief colliding with impossible hope.

chapters.title: What Ada Carried
chapters.summary: Ada reveals she was Julian's landlady's daughter abroad; he entrusted her with letters and a promise involving a German family, the Brandts. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: fear of being disbelieved.

chapters.title: Letters I Should Not Have Read
chapters.summary: Ivo confesses to Edith that he reads her mail — and that he'd intercepted one of Julian's coded notes months ago, dismissing it as nonsense. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: shame and the first fracture of his detachment.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Edith recalls Julian's 1911 promise to help the Brandts flee if war came. Now he's asking her to honor it from beyond his own grave. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: duty versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Roads to Dover
chapters.summary: The three travel toward the coast following Ada's instructions, while a War Office man, Captain Reeve, begins asking questions in the villages. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: conspiracy becoming real.

chapters.title: The Inn at Hythe
chapters.summary: At a smuggling inn, they meet an old contact of Julian's who confirms he lives — but warns that Reeve suspects desertion, not espionage, which is worse. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the stakes turn personal and criminal.

chapters.title: Coded in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ivo deciphers Julian's method: messages hidden in suffrage circulars he delivered without ever knowing. His whole reading habit was blind. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: vertigo at his own blindness.

chapters.title: Edith's Platform
chapters.summary: At a suffrage rally, Edith must speak while knowing her brother's survival could destroy her credibility. Reeve watches from the crowd. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: public performance over private terror.

chapters.title: Ada's Own War
chapters.summary: Ada's backstory surfaces: her father was interned as an enemy alien despite decades in England; Julian promised to help her find him too. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: anger at a country that made her stateless.

chapters.title: The First Summons
chapters.summary: Reeve formally interviews Ivo about suspicious mail. Ivo lies smoothly for the first time in his life and hates how easily it comes. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: complicity settling on him like a coat.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Signal Box
chapters.summary: Following a new coded message, they retrieve a package at a railway signal box: money, papers, and a photograph of Julian alive, older, bearded. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: proof transforming doubt into mission.

chapters.title: The Brandt Letters
chapters.summary: The package contains the Brandts' desperate plea: their son faces deportation to a reprisal camp. The promise now has a deadline. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: abstract promise becomes flesh-and-blood urgency.

chapters.title: An Enemy's Face
chapters.summary: Ivo meets Herr Brandt working covertly on a Kentish farm and confronts his own casual prejudices. They share tea in silence. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: 'enemy' dissolving into a tired man's face.

chapters.title: Reeve Closes In
chapters.summary: Reeve searches Marlowe House under pretense of security review. Edith hides Julian's letters inside her suffrage archives, betting on sexist assumptions. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: weaponizing contempt.

chapters.title: The Quarrel
chapters.summary: Ada wants to cross to France immediately; Edith insists on legal channels; Ivo sides with Ada. The found family fractures over method. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: belonging threatened by its first real fight.

chapters.title: What Ivo Read
chapters.summary: Alone with Edith's private diary-letters, Ivo learns she knew about his reading all along and let him continue, trusting him. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into devotion.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: The innkeeper agrees to arrange a channel crossing but demands a favor: moving a wounded deserter inland first. A detour with consequences. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: debts compounding.

chapters.title: Moving Mr. Ellery
chapters.summary: The deserter, delirious, mistakes Ivo for his brother and confesses what broke him at the front — echoing Julian's unspoken reasons. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: empathy cracking open his old armor.

chapters.title: Reeve's Offer
chapters.summary: Reeve privately offers Edith a deal: Julian's quiet return for her public withdrawal from the movement. She asks for a night to consider. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: the cause and the blood tied in one knot.

chapters.title: Ada Disappears
chapters.summary: Ada vanishes, leaving a note in Julian's borrowed cipher. Ivo realizes she's gone to make the crossing alone and spare them. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: panic revealing love he hadn't named.

chapters.title: The Chase to Folkestone
chapters.summary: Ivo and Edith race the coast road, dodging Reeve's men, and find Ada detained at the port — her papers flagged. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: terror sharpened by helplessness.

chapters.title: Interrogation Room
chapters.summary: Ada is questioned as a possible spy. She holds to her cover story with a courage that stuns even Reeve. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: identity as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: Julian Writes Directly
chapters.summary: A letter arrives addressed openly to Edith: Julian proposes to surrender in exchange for the Brandts' safe passage, naming Reeve's superior as guarantor. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ivo seeks out a retired archivist who once processed Julian's 'death' paperwork and finds evidence the death report was falsified by someone inside. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the system itself is lying.

chapters.title: Reeve Unmasked
chapters.summary: The falsifier was Reeve's mentor; Reeve has been hunting Julian to bury the scandal, not serve justice. Leverage shifts hands. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: the hunter revealed as the hunted.

chapters.title: Terms at the Chapel
chapters.summary: Edith and Reeve negotiate in a disused chapel: Julian's surrender, the Brandts' passage, Ada's immunity, and Edith's continued silence — not withdrawal. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: power wielded without cruelty.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Ivo drives Ada and the Brandt son through a fog-bound night to a waiting boat, every checkpoint a coin flip. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: white-knuckle solidarity.

chapters.title: Halfway Across
chapters.summary: Mid-channel, the boat is hailed by a patrol; the smuggler's forged papers hold by inches. Ada nearly gives herself up to save the boy. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused by friendship.

chapters.title: Julian Comes Home
chapters.summary: Julian walks into a Kent police station and surrenders, ending two years of ghosts. Edith watches through glass, forbidden to speak to him. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: grief and joy in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: A closed tribunal weighs desertion against Reeve's buried scandal. Ivo testifies about the letters — reading aloud, at last, honestly. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: his secret skill becomes salvation.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Julian receives a reduced sentence and medical discharge; the scandal quietly retires Reeve. Justice is imperfect but real. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: bitter, grateful compromise.

chapters.title: Winter at Marlowe House
chapters.summary: Julian convalesces; Ada stays on as Edith's secretary; the house fills with arguments and laughter again. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: found family knitting closed.

chapters.title: News from Across the Water
chapters.summary: A letter confirms the Brandts reached safety; Ada's father, traced through the same channels, is alive in Holland. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: hope arriving cautiously.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: New Year's Eve, 1916 into 1917. The household keeps vigil; Julian burns his false names; Ivo makes a resolution he doesn't say aloud. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: threshold, literal and figurative.

chapters.title: What History Owes
chapters.summary: Edith publishes an anonymous account of the affair, changing only names — her act of faith that truth can survive telling. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: testimony as inheritance.

chapters.title: Ivo's Letter
chapters.summary: For the first time, Ivo writes a letter instead of merely carrying others': to Ada, clumsy and honest, asking her to stay. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: vulnerability chosen freely.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: They plant a new orchard behind Marlowe House — one tree for each person lost, saved, or forgiven. Ada teaches Julian the grafting she learned abroad. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: rootedness after uprooting.

chapters.title: Ada and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Years later framing device: Ada, grown older, walks the orchard with Ivo and tells a child the story we've just read. History, she says, happened to us. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: inheritance passed on, identity at peace.
